page.layout: One column of text on one printed page, with a ruled line and an ornamental border dividing the sections. Above the rule: a continued paragraph, a numbered thesis, an italic passage with a citation, and a closing line. Below the rule: a problem heading, a section heading with Greek, and a numbered list of questions. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right. No running head.

main_text.p: cessarium; tum ut boni, spe præmij, honorum videlicet & dignitatum, in virtutis amore conseruentur & incitentur; mali vero formidine pœnæ, contineantur in officio, arceanturq;. Arist. 5. Polit.

Inter leges vero, Salus populi, Conseruatio Vniuersitatis, suprema lex in Repub. esto. Quarū inuetione, expo-sitionem, & demum constituendarum rationem uniuer-sam, ipsa IVRISPRVDENTIA ulterius persequitur.
main_text.head: PROBLEMA. Vbi Medicus incipiat, ubi Theologus?
CONSECTARIA SEV Πορίσματα quinq;
main_text.p: AN Contemplatiua, an Actiua vita sit præferen-da?
Quanta debeat esse multitudo ad conuenientem Ciuitatis magnitudinem?
An Regem Legemue dominari melius sit?
An ab optimo Viro regi, vel ab optimis Legibus gubernari magis expediat?
Virtus absolute boni viri, & boni ciuis, num sit eadem, an alia?

page.notes: Printed "XLIIX." is probably a misprint for XLIX; kept as printed. The symbol before "Moralis" in the italic closing line is a small ornamental glyph, not transcribed. The word "inuetione" is copied as printed, and I could not confirm a mark above it. Faint mirrored text (show-through) at the right edge and top was left out. Greek heading copied as printed. The ornamental border was not transcribed.
